title: Featured: codeSplitter
intro: The code host for the agentic era, and the reason a lot of the rest exists. [Try it](https://codesplitter.notryanquinn.workers.dev).

apps.name: codeSplitter
apps.line: A code host for the agentic era: every file a Durable Object, agents editing line by line, real git on Cloudflare Artifacts, an MCP server, on the edge and as a desktop app from one codebase. [Try it](https://codesplitter.notryanquinn.workers.dev)

title: Games
intro: The fun ones. Most play in the browser, and every one runs as a desktop app. Most recently worked on first.

apps.name: Mythic Masters
apps.line: A 3D creature arena brawler where mass, height and stats shape each body, flyers have to come down, and a headless bot-vs-bot tuner keeps 76 folklore beasts, from a 6 kg jackalope to a tonne of lake monster, each winning about half its fights; one arena layout wearing a skin per built region, on a route of 64 folklore regions

apps.name: Hippo Tycoon
apps.line: One game class runs as a Durable Object on Cloudflare and in-process in the binary: solo, couch, LAN party and online rooms

apps.name: Splat Spray
apps.line: The smallest one: a three.js game with no backend at all, made a desktop app by a ten-line config

apps.name: Skate Tech Park
apps.line: Skate a street spot, or take a rocket roadster with ten cold-gas thrusters over the gap: a three.js page on a pure fixed-step sim the tests drive headless

apps.name: Park Hide & Seek
apps.line: 3D hide and seek on real Yosemite terrain, played by the page, by a LAN host or by the edge; each player is sent only what they can see. [Play it](https://park-hide-seek.notryanquinn.workers.dev)

apps.name: Alien Disc Golf
apps.line: Disc golf where the course is the planet: nine holes between random countries on a three.js globe, the disc carried by NOAA's real wind right now (the Worker relays the latest GFS grid from NOMADS, the page decodes the GRIB2), a lofted throw riding the jet stream; guess which country you're teeing off from for a stroke back

apps.name: Two Fronts
apps.line: Thunder Marines vs the Wooka horde: a turn-based galactic war plus three.js hero battles in orbit and on six worlds, one per kind of sector (redwood forest, desert, ruined city, glowing alien night, beach, deep-space station), built apart and joined by small JSON types (a spec in, a result out); play the AI or hotseat in the page, or a friend online through a Durable Object per campaign

apps.name: Git Recon
apps.line: A repo as a shooter level: its folders become compounds and its files buildings on real ground (Yosemite, or any lat/long) or a plastic-army kitchen and garden, fought with git commands as weapons, in the page on your own, up to 64 to a battle over the LAN, or online in a Durable Object per room

apps.name: Delayed Reaction
apps.line: A phone-first rhythm game: you sprint down a rolling neon tunnel, a ring calls a note, you answer it a bar later on one of four thumb pads, and your answers echo back through a dub delay; the sim plays in beats with no page, so a test runs every level

apps.name: Excalibrawl
apps.line: An hourly drawing fight: Clef vs Clef Flash picking only a move, shape, colour, grid cell and size from a picture of their halves, or two text models writing a token-cheap drawing language, with Clef as referee, for two cents or less a fight; replays and a live socket in R2 and a Durable Object

title: One account, one front door
intro: What ties the apps together: one sign-in for all of them, and one page that lists them.

apps.name: eqosys
apps.line: Your home for every Q game: your games, friends, saves and studio on one account. Under it, Better Auth on D1, a PKCE code handoff to each app with a signed token it can check alone, which app each person came from and what they may do in each, and a Durable Object a person for friends, presence and notifications. Also a plain OpenID provider, so a site's own Better Auth or a native app signs in with it

apps.name: Qollab
apps.line: Realtime rooms for any app on Cloudflare: rooms, seats, parties, presence and saves in one call. Built into eqosys as a Worker of its own, with a Durable Object a player and a room

apps.name: Playground
apps.line: One page that lists every app with a way to try it: Play, Download or Source. Static assets only, so it bills nothing

title: My apps
intro: Real tools for real work, some under their own license.

apps.name: ShareSplat
apps.line: Product photos to a 3D spin for a store page: a guided phone shot list (six sides for an AI-guessed mesh, or 72 photos in rings for a real Gaussian splat) and a turntable splat viewer with a paste-in Shopify embed

apps.name: qCRM
apps.line: A CRM with MCP built in, a Rust wasm engine in the browser, office sync, signed webhooks and a desktop build; roles for a real place and hashed org ids. QNTBR-licensed.

apps.name: GeoBoxQ
apps.line: Shipping box fit checker with a Rust engine that packs boxes inside boxes. Private license.

apps.name: GeoBoxQ for Shopify
apps.line: A small wrapper that turns a Shopify cart into the store's own box.

apps.name: artstewengine
apps.line: A tiny RWSDK app on D1 with a Better Auth admin page: add who has paid, and qCRM's sealed engine gets its key only for a paid license

apps.name: What Would Fantano Say
apps.line: A parody music critic as an RWSDK Worker: the phone decodes the song and picks a 15 s clip, and Cloudflare's Clef-omni judges it for about $5 per 100,000 reviews, behind a rate limit, Turnstile, an edge cache and a daily budget

apps.name: AT Lens
apps.line: Type a handle and watch the AT Protocol work: domain to DID to data server to typed records, checked both ways, then the account live on the Jetstream firehose; sign in with atproto OAuth to write a record of our own Lexicon and watch it come back; no keys, no bindings

apps.name: One Team in 32
apps.line: One static page ("One Team in 32") served from a Cloudflare Worker as plain assets, no Worker code

title: The workshop
intro: Music, 3D and circuits: tools for making things, with a Rust engine beside a TypeScript one where it pays.

apps.name: FM Groovebox
apps.line: One Rust crate as wasm in the audio thread and over FFI on the host, bit-identical to the TypeScript engine

apps.name: Splat Rooms
apps.line: A splat hunting game with a world class and 30 MB scenes streamed from a folder on your disk, never embedded

apps.name: Auto Rig
apps.line: Auto-rigging a 3D model in Rust and TypeScript with identical output

apps.name: Meshy Studio
apps.line: A folder-based batch tool for Meshy's API (image, multi-image and text to 3D, texture, remesh, rig, animate, concept art): your key stays local, every spend is priced first

apps.name: Motion MIDI
apps.line: One synth in Rust and in TypeScript, checked sample by sample

apps.name: Splat Desktop
apps.line: PlayCanvas' SuperSplat editor as a desktop app working on a folder on your disk

apps.name: tscircuit Desktop
apps.line: A heavy, real-world Vite app as one file, with a Rust engine up to 22x faster and a TypeScript fallback

apps.name: Pixel RAG
apps.line: Drop in your screenshots and find the parts that look alike across all of them. One Rust index shared by every worker, web or desktop.

title: Everything else: frameworks, other people's apps and test fixtures
intro: A framework's own sample app, or someone else's app, run with its code unchanged, plus the small apps the tests lean on. A new app lands here first, until it's moved to its section.

apps.name: Agent Office
apps.line: Someone else's Node server (PTYs, WebSockets, a 3D client) as one binary, nothing forked

apps.name: TerraViz
apps.line: TerraViz, The Zyra Project's Science On a Sphere globe (Apache-2.0, not ours), cloned and run with its code unchanged, plus Shared Sphere on top: a room on one globe, a teacher's lock so a class follows one pair of hands, NOAA tour scripts kept in step on every screen and read as slides by a small Rust crate

apps.name: Nuxt
apps.line: A Nuxt 4 app on Nitro's `cloudflare-module` preset (one KV binding) as a desktop app with no edits: `init` reads it and the host runs the Worker Nitro built; the same shared HTTP journey checks it

apps.name: Qwik City
apps.line: A Qwik City app on its own `cloudflare-pages` adapter (a `routeLoader$` and a `routeAction$` counting in KV through `platform.env`) as a desktop app with no edits; `init` reads the adapter's `dist/_worker.js` as it is

apps.name: Astro
apps.line: An Astro site on `@astrojs/cloudflare` (a server page and an API route counting in KV through `cloudflare:workers`) as a desktop app with no edits, and `init` reads it as it is

apps.name: Elysia
apps.line: An Elysia Worker as Elysia's Cloudflare guide writes it (`aot: false`, `cloudflare:workers`) as a desktop app with no edits, and `init` now reads Elysia

apps.name: SvelteKit
apps.line: A SvelteKit 3 app on the Cloudflare adapter (a `load` from KV, a form action that bumps it) as a desktop app with no edits: the same sample app contract as hono-example, checked by the same shared journey

apps.name: SolidStart
apps.line: A SolidStart 2 app on Nitro's `cloudflare_module` preset (a `"use server"` query and an API route counting in KV through `cloudflare:workers`) as a desktop app with no edits, and `rustybuns init` reads it as it is.

apps.name: React Router
apps.line: React Router 7 on Cloudflare's own template (`workers/app.ts`, the Vite plugin, a loader and an action over KV) as a desktop app with no edits: the second framework on the shared sample-app journey

apps.name: Next.js
apps.line: A Next.js 16 app on `@opennextjs/cloudflare` (one KV binding) as a desktop app with no edits: `init` reads it and the host runs the `worker.js` OpenNext built; the same shared HTTP journey checks it

apps.name: Svelte SPA
apps.line: A client-only Svelte 5 + Vite app (no server) as a desktop app, its counter in a `"use server"` action the host runs.

apps.name: Hono
apps.line: A Hono Worker from Hono's own docs (one KV binding) as a desktop app with no edits: the sample app contract every framework example meets, checked by one shared HTTP journey

apps.name: Elysia RealWorld
apps.line: bedstack's RealWorld backend (Elysia, Drizzle, postgres.js) with no source edits: a desktop binary on PGlite that passes their Postman suite, and the five ways it breaks on Workers

apps.name: TanStack Start
apps.line: TanStack Start on Cloudflare's Vite plugin (server functions, a server route, D1 and KV) as a desktop app, its code unchanged

apps.name: Hello World
apps.line: The first five minutes: a twenty-line page that the welcome tour digs up, lets three agents rewrite at once, then asks why not deploy it

apps.name: Agent Demo
apps.line: A small snack-vote Worker seeded into codeSplitter, so several coding agents can build it at once and settle a merge conflict on camera

apps.name: Borg Postgres
apps.line: A Postgres app keeps its database and moves its code: Hyperdrive on the edge, PGlite on the desktop.

apps.name: Borg
apps.line: Not an app: a small Worker that uses every binding once, so one suite can check the local twins against a real deploy

apps.name: SPA fixture
apps.line: Not an app: a slice of a real RWSDK game that the tests use to check `init` reads it right

apps.name: Worker example
apps.line: A whole Worker (D1, KV, a Durable Object) as a desktop binary in half a second, plus a Rust FFI probe with a TypeScript fallback
